name: Nelson Gallagher
life: “I still remember reading cufflinks as if they were tiny portraits.” Sunday often includes a stop at Paper & Pine Books, where Nelson starts with the handwritten shelf cards and often leaves with a suggestion for somebody else.
voice: I left cufflinks on the card and came back to find someone had paired them with shoelaces.
appearance: Nelson has a swept fringe and a closely clipped nape, two dimples that appear only with a full smile, and a favorite piece of clothing, a mustard canvas overshirt. It usually goes with a comb in a sleeve sewn into the lining. When somebody else has the floor, Nelson listens with the head tilted a little to the left.
personality: Nelson can be wonderfully decisive about an emergency and maddeningly undecided about a gift. This is because a person can say precisely what hurts and rarely says exactly what they want.
agenda: To return the cufflinks to somebody who will wear them.
family: Vera Gallagher is Nelson’s half-sibling. Nelson chooses an ordinary story to tell. Vera asks the question the rest of the family avoided. They tend to get further with an important subject when it arrives in the middle of talk about dinner or work. Asked about *Reading the payslip*, Vera says, “I learned to read novels at fifty. Numbers with brackets still make me sweat.”
connections: Celia Lai. They put the largest easy fastening where the person who needs it can actually reach. Also in the story is Lola Jeong (button collector).
